sourceOccurrences.label: First-exit decomposition and the boundary functional
sourceOccurrences.locator: Named statement start lines in the pinned source: 24, 42, 75, 101, 126, 139, 145, 161, 185
sourceOccurrences.note: ROY9 covers finite-domain escape, infinite-cluster comparison, singleton and zero-boundary cases. 6J9C supplies the exact ray escape and boundary sums, with both endpoint parameters. Its discussion retains deterministic first exit on arbitrary domains and independence for a countable domain in an arbitrary ambient space. The two source representations of the boundary sum describe the same nonnegative quantity.

sourceOccurrences.label: Prescribed finite cluster and the law outside it
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit additional deductions
sourceOccurrences.note: R3I9 records the exact event decomposition and countable product-law factorization. E7R2 records independence from strictly exterior measurable events and the induced-exterior connection formula. The boundary product and conditional-law interpretation are extra consequences. Internal connectivity has a finite-coordinate measurability argument even without countable ambient vertices; the source exports its measurability under Countable V. Existing boundary and first-exit records are unchanged.

sourceOccurrences.label: Cluster exploration and boundary contraction
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: The source proves restricted first exit by exposing the internal cluster and taking its last exit, using disjoint coordinate blocks. Uniform contraction is solved in finite induced domains before exhaustion; the finite susceptibility is never assumed.

sourceOccurrences.note: Collapse preserves the product intensity law when each pair fibre has summable intensity. Ghost connection detects escape; agreement of original and collapsed internal connections requires that the root not reach the ghost.
